title: POST /tasks accepts non-string values in the tags array
body:
## What happens

`POST /tasks` with a `tags` array containing numbers is accepted and stored:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:3000/tasks \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title": "Ship it", "tags": [1, 2, 3]}'
```

Returns `201` and the stored task has `"tags": [1, 2, 3]`.

## What should happen

The `Task` interface in `src/types.ts` declares `tags: string[]`, so storing numbers breaks the type contract. Any consumer that calls a string method on a tag will throw at runtime.

The request should be rejected with `400` and an error naming the problem, consistent with the existing validation style in this route.

## Notes

- The current check is `Array.isArray(body.tags)`, which confirms the container but not the element type.
- `PUT /tasks/:id` has the same gap and should be fixed too.
- Empty arrays are valid and must keep working.
expected_behaviour: POST and PUT reject tags arrays containing any non-string element with HTTP 400. Empty arrays and all-string arrays continue to be accepted.
notes: Validation gap confirmed against sample-app: Array.isArray passes but element types are unchecked, while types.ts declares string[].
